narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and your job type. The short nine-month duration you asked for actually worked in your favor. Most approved applicants request loans lasting about 19 months, so your shorter term pushed the prediction toward approval. However, this positive effect was outweighed by two other important factors.

Your checking account status of less than 0 DM was the strongest reason for denial. Only 12.6% of approved applicants have a negative balance, while the majority maintain positive balances or no account at all. This signaled higher risk to the model. Your job as a management, self-employed, or highly skilled professional also pulled the prediction toward bad credit risk, even though this group represents 16.5% of approved loans.

Taken together, these elements led the bank to decline your application. To improve your chances next time, focus on building a positive checking account balance before reapplying and consider whether a slightly longer loan term might better align with patterns the model sees in successful applicants. You may also want to explore improving other areas of your credit profile in the meantime. (218 words)
